quick-start.title: zoxide Quick Start Guide
quick-start.excerpt: Get started with zoxide in 5 minutes, learn basic commands and configuration methods.
quick-start.author: zoxide.org
quick-start.content:
# zoxide Quick Start Guide

zoxide is a smart directory jumper written in Rust with exceptional performance. This guide will help you get started in 5 minutes.

## Installing zoxide

### macOS
\`\`\`bash
brew install zoxide
\`\`\`

### Windows
\`\`\`bash
scoop install zoxide
\`\`\`

### Linux / All Platforms
\`\`\`bash
cargo install zoxide
\`\`\`

## Shell Configuration

After installation, you need to add the initialization command to your Shell configuration file.

### zsh
Add to \`~/.zshrc\`:
\`\`\`bash
eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"
\`\`\`

### bash
Add to \`~/.bashrc\`:
\`\`\`bash
eval "$(zoxide init bash)"
\`\`\`

### fish
Add to \`~/.config/fish/config.fish\`:
\`\`\`fish
zoxide init fish | source
\`\`\`

## Basic Usage

After configuration, reload your Shell or open a new terminal window to start using zoxide.

### Basic Commands

- \`z <directory>\` - Jump to matching directory
- \`zi <directory>\` - Interactive directory selection (with fuzzy search)
- \`z -\` - Return to previous directory
- \`z -l\` - List all matching directories

### Examples

\`\`\`bash
# Jump to directory containing "project"
z project

# Interactive directory selection
zi pro

# Return to previous directory
z -
\`\`\`

## Advanced Tips

### Excluding Directories

Use the \`_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS\` environment variable to exclude directories from indexing:

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var"
\`\`\`

### Custom Database Location

By default, the database is stored in \`~/.zo\`. You can customize it with \`_ZO_DATA_DIR\`:

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/zoxide"
\`\`\`

## Summary

zoxide makes directory navigation simple and efficient. With smart learning and fuzzy search, you can quickly jump to any directory without typing the full path.

For more advanced usage, check out the [Advanced Configuration Tutorial](/tutorials/advanced-config).

advanced-config.title: zoxide Advanced Configuration Tips
advanced-config.excerpt: Learn how to configure zoxide to improve productivity, including alias settings, directory exclusion, etc.
advanced-config.author: zoxide.org
advanced-config.content:
# zoxide Advanced Configuration Tips

zoxide provides rich configuration options that allow you to customize your experience according to your needs.

## Environment Variable Configuration

### Excluding Directories

Use \`_ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS\` to exclude directories from indexing, improving performance:

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/node_modules"
\`\`\`

Multiple directories are separated by colons.

### Custom Database Location

By default, the database is stored in the \`.zo\` file in your home directory. You can customize it with \`_ZO_DATA_DIR\`:

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/zoxide"
\`\`\`

### Maximum History Age

Use \`_ZO_MAXAGE\` to set the maximum history age in days (default 10000):

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_MAXAGE=5000
\`\`\`

## Alias Settings

zoxide supports custom aliases to make common commands shorter:

\`\`\`bash
# Add to Shell config file
alias zz='z'
alias zi='zi'
alias za='zoxide add'
alias zq='zoxide query'
\`\`\`

## Integration with fzf

Combining with fzf enables more powerful directory search and selection:

\`\`\`bash
# Add to ~/.zshrc
zi() {
  local dir
  dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf) && z "$dir"
}
\`\`\`

## Performance Optimization

### Reducing Index Range

Only indexing commonly used directories can significantly improve performance:

\`\`\`bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/proc:/sys"
\`\`\`

### Regular Database Cleanup

If the database is too large, you can manually clean it:

\`\`\`bash
# Check database size
ls -lh ~/.zo

# Delete database to start fresh (use with caution)
rm ~/.zo
\`\`\`

## Team Collaboration

zoxide supports shared databases, allowing team members to share common directories:

\`\`\`bash
# Use shared database location
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="/shared/path/zoxide"
\`\`\`

## Summary

With proper configuration, zoxide can better adapt to your workflow. We recommend starting by excluding unnecessary directories and gradually optimizing the configuration.

For more configuration options, check out the [official documentation](https://github.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide).

zoxide-vs-autojump.title: zoxide vs autojump Performance Comparison
zoxide-vs-autojump.excerpt: Detailed comparison of the performance differences and user experience between zoxide and autojump.
zoxide-vs-autojump.author: zoxide.org
zoxide-vs-autojump.content:
# zoxide vs autojump Performance Comparison

zoxide and autojump are both smart directory jump tools, but they have significant differences in performance, features, and usability.

## Performance Comparison

### Startup Speed

zoxide is written in Rust and starts extremely fast:

- **zoxide**: ~5ms startup time
- **autojump**: ~50ms startup time

zoxide is **10x faster** than autojump.

### Query Speed

In large project directories, zoxide's query speed is also significantly faster:

- **zoxide**: Fuzzy search < 10ms
- **autojump**: Query time 20-50ms

## Feature Comparison

### Fuzzy Search

- **zoxide**: ✅ Supports fuzzy search, no need for full path
- **autojump**: ❌ No fuzzy search support

### Interactive Selection

- **zoxide**: ✅ Supports \`zi\` command for interactive selection
- **autojump**: ❌ Not supported

### Learning Algorithm

- **zoxide**: ✅ Smart learning algorithm, gets more accurate with use
- **autojump**: ✅ Basic frequency statistics

## Usability Comparison

### Command Simplicity

zoxide's commands are more concise:

\`\`\`bash
# zoxide
z project

# autojump
j project
\`\`\`

### Configuration Complexity

- **zoxide**: Simple configuration, just one initialization command
- **autojump**: Requires additional Shell integration configuration

## Cross-Platform Support

- **zoxide**: ✅ Supports macOS, Linux, Windows
- **autojump**: ✅ Supports macOS, Linux (limited Windows support)

## Maintenance Status

- **zoxide**: Very active, continuous updates
- **autojump**: Slower updates

## Summary

| Feature | zoxide | autojump |
|---------|--------|----------|
| Performance | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐ |
| Fuzzy Search | ✅ | ❌ |
| Interactive Selection | ✅ | ❌ |
| Cross-platform | ✅ | ✅ |
| Maintenance Status | Active | Slow |

**Conclusion**: If you're looking for performance and modern experience, zoxide is the better choice. If you're already used to autojump, migrating to zoxide is also simple.

Check out the [full comparison](/comparisons) for more details.
